name: River-mouth adaptation kit for hydro-grade debris booms
description: A lighter, modular version of the log-screen boom engineering Ecocoast/Bolina already runs at African hydropower dams (Cahora Bassa, Mozambique; Kariba, Zambia), re-sited at river mouths rather than turbine intakes, with a sorting gate to separate plastic from woody debris and route plastic to a buyback or recycling depot on the model already running at RiverImpact's Motagua barrier and TheLitterboomProject's South African rivers.
addresses: The report's standing finding that interception hardware sized for Africa's river systems is nearly absent from the map. Ecocoast's dam-grade booms prove the engineering works on large, high-debris tropical rivers, but every current African deployment protects infrastructure, not the ocean; adapting the same hardware to river mouths would close that specific gap rather than just adding a second hydro-protection entry.
